rounds.text: Amiable Logistics India Ltd trades at a compelling valuation of 13.4x P/E and 1.23x price-to-book, sitting below sector benchmarks of 18.85x and 1.39x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. The structural earnings capability shines through a superior return on capital employed (ROCE) of 12.88% and return on equity (ROE) of 10.12%, both easily outperforming sector medians [E8, E9, E10, E69]. Furthermore, intrinsic value estimates via discounted cash flow analysis point to a substantial margin of safety of 68.7%, with the current share price implying a mere 2.3% earnings growth expectation [E38, E39, E40]. Balance sheet health is solid, highlighted by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x alongside a reduction in total borrowings, while positive operating and free cash flows underscore genuine cash generation [E31, E33, E34]. Insider alignment is equally encouraging, as promoters have increased their stake by a full percentage point to 70.16% [E36]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has contracted over trailing and 3-year periods alongside an inconsistent operating margin trend [E15, E16, E28].

The bull case rests on statistical cheapness, but the underlying top-line reality is contracting sharply across multiple horizons. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -16% [E16], and 3-year compounded sales growth is -14% [E15], demonstrating a persistent inability to expand revenue. This top-line contraction bleeds into operational efficiency, where the yearly operating-margin trend is flagged as inconsistent [E27] and the quarterly operating margin dropped to 3% in Mar 2026 from 7% in the year-ago quarter [E26]. Furthermore, reported earnings quality is heavily distorted because the earnings profile includes Rs 1.50 Cr of other income [E55], masking core operational weakness. Shareholder returns are further undermined by a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], poor historical return on equity averaging 11.7% over the last 3 years [E54], and a ballooning debtor days metric that has worsened from 32.2 to 44.0 days [E56]. Conceded: [E38].

Conceded: [E16] and [E15]. Despite top-line contraction, the company's profitability has proven resilient with a 5-year compounded profit growth of 27% [E17] and a 20% surge over the trailing twelve months [E19]. While the bear highlights margin inconsistency and a drop in quarterly operating margin [E26, E27], the business maintains superior capital efficiency with an ROA of 7.54%, ROE of 10.12%, and ROCE of 12.88%, all comfortably outperforming their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10]. Addressing the concern over other income [E55], the firm nevertheless generated positive free cash flow of Rs 0.35 Cr alongside an operating cash flow representing 149% of operating profit in March 2026 [E31, E32]. Conceded: [E4] and [E56]. Even with those operational hurdles, the balance sheet remains exceptionally strong with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x and reduced borrowings [E33, E34], while insiders who know the business best have actually increased their stake to 70.16% [E36].

Conceded: [E17] and [E19] regarding historical profit growth. However, the bull's reliance on bottom-line figures is deeply misleading when earnings quality is severely compromised by ₹1.50 Cr of other income [E55]. Furthermore, pointing to capital efficiency ratios like an ROE of 10.12% [E9] or ROCE of 12.88% [E10] ignores the company's own official assessment that it suffers from a low return on equity of 11.7% over the last 3 years [E54]. The bull dismisses rising debtor days, but the evidence shows a direct drag on working capital as debtor days worsened from 32.2 to 44.0 days [E56]. Conceded: [E31] and [E32] for recent cash flows. Yet this positive generation clashes with a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.38x in March 2026, indicating that profits are running far ahead of actual cash and warranting scrutiny on receivables and accruals [E29]. Finally, praising a stable debt-to-equity ratio [E33, E34] completely sidesteps the alarming core contraction in top-line demand, evidenced by a 3-year sales decline of -14% [E15] and a trailing twelve-month sales drop of -16% [E16].
